label: DERIVED from the committed ENG1 step model; NOT measured in this row
assumptions: one escalation call is one N1 Nexar request of 378 prompt tokens with one image, entering the engine as a single prefill request in its own step

the step model is evaluated at tok = 378, images_in_step = 1, prefill_reqs = 1, decode_reqs = 0 and ctx = tok, which is the isolated-call reading of a model fitted on BUSY intervals; the ENG1 report measured the engine to be SUB-LINEAR in batched small prefills (16-batch / 16 x single = 0.51 at N = 1), so a batched fleet would fit MORE devices than this column states and the column is a LOWER bound in that respect

the device count is a pure throughput bound at 100 % accelerator utilization: queueing is ignored, so the 0.395 s cloud latency is NOT guaranteed at the stated count. The in-flight column is Little's law at that arrival rate and is what the latency budget would have to accommodate
the admission-stall column charges each call the measured multimodal admission stall (12.7 ms + 1.1 ms per image) as if no two calls shared a step, which is the pessimistic end
every device is assumed to run the same workload at the same budget, with no correlation between devices' escalation times; correlated escalation bursts would reduce the count
the ENG1 step model was fitted on the H100 NVL (sn4622120321) and on Part A and Part B E0 steps only; Part C and the HOLDOUT were not used in the fit
interpretation: the budget is a TEST VARIABLE standing for cloud spare capacity (D58). Read as load: 5 % of the call rate is about 144 devices per H100 and 40 % about 18, so the budget axis is a fleet-size axis, and the cells at 5 to 20 % are the ones a shared H100 could actually serve.
